VA disability ratings don't add up like ordinary arithmetic — they use the "whole person" efficiency formula from 38 CFR § 4.25.

Bilateral factor (38 CFR § 4.26): the paired wrist conditions are combined and boosted first, even though back (40%) is your highest-rated condition individually — the pairing rule applies regardless of rank.
  Step 1: Combine 10% and 10% wrists — remaining efficiency after 10% is 90%. 10% of 90% ≈ 9, so 10 + 9 = 19.
  Step 2: Apply the 10% bilateral boost: 19 × 1.1 ≈ 21 (rounded).

Rank all conditions, highest to lowest:
- back: 40%
- bilateral wrists (combined + boosted): 21%

  Step 3: Remaining efficiency is 60%. 21% of that ≈ 13, so 40 + 13 = 53.

Exact combined value before rounding: 53%. Per 38 CFR § 4.25, that rounds to a final combined rating of 50%.
Note: pyramiding rules (38 CFR § 4.14) mean each of these must represent a distinct disabling manifestation, not the same symptom rated twice under different codes.
